source.title: A Geometric View for Understanding Concept Learning and Neuron Interpretation in Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Chenhao Zhang; Chris Lin; Su-In Lee

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies synthetic SAE concept learning and neuron-interpretation correspondence, but does not measure the audit shares, held-out explanation faithfulness, or other specific outcomes named in V1–V7.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on concept alignment and the disagreement between concept learning and neuron interpretation in synthetic data. These are related to neuron interpretation, but are not the specific measures named by the claim versions. Results cited from other work were not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study trains ReLU and Top-K SAEs on two-dimensional synthetic clusters and measures set-alignment F1 and a concept-learning/neuron-interpretation disagreement ratio. It audits no language-model or vision-model neurons. It reports no share of neurons with one job and no held-out simulation scores of neuron explanations. It builds no attribution graphs and does not examine InceptionV1. None of its results bear on V1–V7. The finding that a unit's best-matching concept may differ from the target (reverse-map disagreement) is conceptually near V6, but it is measured on synthetic SAE latents with ground-truth clusters, not on natural-language explanations of model neurons. It therefore goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also conclude that wider SAEs improve concept learning by providing more candidate features, with gains plateauing around expansion factor 16. They note that excessive sparsity can hurt concepts needing multiple features, and that the disagreement analysis is preliminary and on synthetic data only.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a geometric/set-alignment framework and synthetic ReLU and Top-K SAE experiments; it does not reproduce either original source's neuron-explanation audit or automated explanation scoring.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with concept type (disjoint or overlapping), task (separation or approximation), SAE architecture (ReLU or Top-K), expansion factor, L0, and number of selected neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: On synthetic 2D clusters, single SAE neurons perfectly separate neuron-separable concepts (F1=1). For non-convex or overlapping concepts, single neurons score F1 0.28–0.78 and multi-neuron units 0.63–0.96.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In synthetic SAE settings, single neurons often fail to align with complex or overlapping concepts, while multi-neuron intersections improve alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Disagreement between the forward concept-to-unit map and the reverse unit-to-concept map falls as expansion factor rises. Overall it goes from 0.69 at EF=2 to 0.10 at EF=64. It stays 0.20–0.31 for overlapping concepts even at EF=64. Disagreement concentrates at intermediate F1 (Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In synthetic SAEs, a unit selected to represent a concept need not be best interpreted as that concept, especially when concepts overlap; wider SAEs reduce but do not eliminate this mismatch.

record.problems: Experiments use controlled two-dimensional synthetic clusters and trained SAEs, not language-model neurons. The disagreement analysis is described as preliminary. Results are averaged over L0 and seeds in Table 1, with no uncertainty estimates stated.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, omitted Table 1's overlapping-concept/approximation entries for Top-K SAE at expansion factors 64 and the remaining Table 2 disagreement-by-F1-interval results; these are in Table 1 and Table 2. Also omitted figure-only curve values and further results not stated numerically in the text.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or job-share proportions.
No language models of any size or architecture audited.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron analysis.
No interpretable-share estimates across tools or architectures in real models. Expansion-factor effects are on synthetic SAEs only.
No attribution graphs or replacement-model comparison.
No explanations from activating examples tested on held-out activations.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: All rows correctly carry versions ["none"] and state cannot_determine, because none measures what a claim version names. The paper cites Bills et al. 2023, an original source, only as background on activating-example interpretation. Rows are synthetic-SAE results and are acceptable as recorded. The Table 1 'All' row (0.69 to 0.10 across expansion factors) was not recorded but is not needed for any version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B neuron poles or report proportions of poles with one job, two related jobs, or unknown jobs.
Does not audit language models across model sizes, dense/MoE architectures, or trillion-parameter scales.
Does not examine InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons or test pose/recursive-generalization versus superposition.
Does not estimate interpretability shares for InceptionV1-sized vision models or compare tools and architectures in that setting.
Does not build attribution graphs or test whether a model's own neurons explain behaviour without a replacement model.
Does not test explanations written from activating examples against held-out activations.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.
